newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to regulate domestic sugar market - minister.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to regulate domestic sugar market - minister.

text.p: Ukraine will take the first steps towards reducing its domestic sugar surplus by limiting the amount of sugar available locally and selling the rest abroad, Agriculture Minister Mykhailo Zubets said on Wednesday.

Zubets, who is also deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture, said the government passed a resolution stating that only 1.5 million tonnes of sugar would be available for sale domestically, at a fixed price, for one year starting on September 1.
"We are implementing quotas on the sugar market," Zubets said. "Ukraine was always a 'sugar nation', but in recent times it has lost its sugar market."

Zubets, who was attending a meeting of a special intergovernmental and private-sector committee for implementing reform in the farm sector said, "We make so much sugar that it's not needed by other countries and it's not needed domestically. The price has dropped steeply, and somehow we have to survive."
Ukraine has forecast this year's sugar output as unchanged from last year's 3.26 million tonnes. It produced 3.49 million tonnes in 1995.
Domestic demand is about 1.5 million tonnes a year.
Zubets said sugar prices would be fixed at 1.19 hryvnias per kg -- double or even triple present domestic prices. Sugar beet growers would also be guaranteed 70 hryvnias per tonne.
"This will help the producer, the government, and the farmer growing the sugar beet, if he meets the quota, to be more effective," Zubets said.
Neighbouring countries like Russia and Belarus, Ukraine's traditional sugar customers, have slapped taxes on imports from Ukraine after accusing it of dumping sugar on their markets.
The minister said this week's planned visit by Russian President Boris Yeltsin could result in the two sides settling their differences over sugar policy.
Zubets said the government would spend the next month devising a method to grant credits to the sugar sector so it could operate within the bounds of the new regulatory regime.
"Now that we have accepted the resolution, the toughest question is where to get money to buy the sugar beets," Zubets said.
There would be no limits on producers selling Ukrainian sugar abroad, he added.
Ukraine had also started to reduce sowing of sugar beets in an effort to reduce domestic supplies, Zubets said.
The Statistics Ministry said Ukraine had nearly completed spring sugar beet sowing having reached 1.164 million hectares this year, compared with 1.3 million hectares in 1996.
"We will not be sowing 1.5 million as in previous years. About 800,000 hectares will be enough to make sugar," Zubets said.
The government resolution also said government departments would put forward suggestions for limiting imports of sugar and related products to Ukraine.
